newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan United Micro up on winning rival's ex-chief.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan United Micro up on winning rival's ex-chief.

text.p: No.2 Taiwan chipmaker United Microelectronics rose at mid-morning on Thursday after giving a senior post to Donald Brooks, who until April was president of No.1 arch rival Taiwan Semiconductor.
After 75 minutes, at 0215 GMT, United Micro was up T$4 or 2.93 percent to T$140.5, while Taiwan Semicon was down T$1.5 or 1.18 percent to T$125.5.
On Wednesday, United Micro said Brooks was named a director of its board and given the post of president of international operations.
Taiwan Semicon said on Thursday its business would not be affected by Brooks' joining its arch rival.
Brokers said Brooks' presence would bring lasting benefits to United Micro's development.
"Of course, Brooks' joining United Micro is positive for the company in the long run," said National Securities analyst Oliver Fang.
"But considering the recent surges in United Micro's share price, I would say it is not cheap now," Fang said.
On the other hand, brokers said Taiwan Semicon was a relatively bargain compared with its rival.
"In terms of price/earnings performance, Taiwan Semicon is apparently undervalued," said indepedent analyst Michael Hung.
Hung estimated United Micro would have earning per share of T$2.82 in 1997 before going ex-bonus issue in late July.
Taiwan Semiconductor, which went ex-bonus in mid-June, already is on track to deliver earnings per share of T$3.92, Hung said.
